Sela
SEE-luh
proper noun
Hebrew Sela, “a rock” or “cliff,” the rock-fortress of Edom.

📖 Biblical Definition

Sela, which means “a rock,” was the great rock-fortress of Edom, a stronghold set among the cliffs of the mountainous land of Esau, all but impregnable to its enemies. When Amaziah king of Judah warred against Edom, he slew ten thousand in the valley of salt and took Sela by war, and called the name of it Joktheel (2Ki 14:7). The prophet Isaiah, in his burden of Moab, bade the fugitives send the lamb of tribute to the ruler of the land “from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion” (Isa 16:1). The rock-city stood for the proud security of Edom, whose dwelling was in the clefts of the rock, who said in his heart, “Who shall bring me down to the ground?” (Obad 3). Yet the LORD declared that though Edom exalt himself as the eagle and set his nest among the stars, from thence He would bring him down (Obad 4). Sela thus became a parable of false security: a fortress that men thought no power could reach, yet which fell under the judgment of God. It witnesses that no rock, however high, can shelter the proud from the hand of the LORD, and that the only sure refuge is the Rock of Ages, the LORD Himself.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The rock-fortress of Edom among the cliffs; a parable of the proud security the LORD brings down.

expand to see more

SELA, the rock-fortress of Edom among the mountain cliffs.

Its name signifies “a rock” or “cliff.”

Amaziah of Judah took it and called it Joktheel (2Ki 14:7).

Isaiah named it in his burden, sending tribute from Sela to Zion (Isa 16:1).

It stood for the proud security of Edom in the clefts of the rock (Obad 3).

📖 Key Scripture

2Ki 14:7 — "He slew of Edom in the valley of salt ten thousand, and took Selah by war, and called the name of it Joktheel unto this day."

Isa 16:1 — "Send ye the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion."

Obad 1:3 — "The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?"

Obad 1:4 — "Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the LORD."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place-name, not a doctrine in dispute; its lesson is that no rock can shelter the proud from the hand of God.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the deceit of pride that dwells in the clefts of the rock and says, “Who shall bring me down?” Edom trusted in the height and strength of Sela, yet the LORD declared He would bring him down though he set his nest among the stars. No fortress of stone or of self-confidence can shelter the proud from the judgment of God; the higher the nest, the greater the fall.

Sela, “the rock,” also turns the heart to the true Rock. Edom’s rock failed him, but there is a Rock that does not fail: “the LORD is my rock, and my fortress” (Ps 18:2). The believer’s safety is not in any stronghold of his own making but in the Rock of Ages, cleft for him. The false security of Sela points by contrast to the only sure refuge of the soul.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name means “a rock” or “cliff,” fitting a fortress hewn among the mountain crags of Edom.

expand to see more

Sela — Hebrew Sela, “a rock” or “cliff.”

It was the rock-fortress of Edom in the mountains of Esau.

Amaziah renamed it Joktheel after taking it by war.

Edom dwelt in the clefts of the rock in proud security.

The false rock of Edom points by contrast to the true Rock, the LORD.

Usage

"Like Edom in Sela, the proud who trust their stronghold are brought down by the hand of God."

"Sela teaches that no fortress of stone or self-confidence shelters the soul from judgment."

"The failing rock of Edom turns the heart to the Rock of Ages, the only sure refuge."
